## Computer Labs {.unnumbered}

Each section's weekly lab meets in a department computer lab
(see [Sections](#sections)).
Outside your lab time, you should be able to use any of the department's open labs,
most of which run the Linux operating system.
Racket is free, so you can also install it on your own computer
(see [Software](#software)).

## Writing to Think {.unnumbered #writing-to-think}

When you are stuck in this course, try putting your question into words in writing.
Write it in full sentences,
with the definitions, proof steps or code you used and what you have already tried.

The habit pays off in two ways.
A written question can be posted on Canvas Discussions (see [Communication](#communication)) so I and others can help.
Writing your thoughts down also helps clarify your question,
and that sometimes answers it.
In an interview on the *5 Minute Mentor* podcast, [Leslie Lamport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leslie_Lamport) says:

> As someone said, "Writing is nature's way of showing you how fuzzy your thinking is."
> If you think you understand something, and don't write down your ideas, you only think you're thinking.
>
> --- Leslie Lamport [@lamport2019think]

The same holds for proofs, which are the writing this course asks of you most.

## Library Writing Resources {.unnumbered}

The Hacherl Research & Writing Studio supports almost anything that involves words:
group projects, essays, posters, podcasts, lab reports, applications, grad theses and more.
You can work with them just like an open art studio or lab space,
where you get work done with feedback along the way.
Drop into the Studio on the second level of Haggard Hall or use their online chat to:

- stay focused and get things done;
- discuss ideas with someone;
- share something you're making;
- ask for tips any time you have difficulty.

See <https://library.wwu.edu/rws> for details.

## Student Conduct {.unnumbered}

I am committed to maintaining an inclusive, supportive, and professional environment
in all academic settings, including lectures, labs, and course-related online spaces.
I expect students to live up to the
[Association for Computing Machinery (ACM) Code of Ethics and Professional Conduct](https://www.acm.org/code-of-ethics),
the ethical code adopted by nearly every software professional.
A pattern of failing to follow the ACM Code of Ethics and Professional Conduct
can negatively affect course grades, up to and including a failing grade for the course.
Conduct is also considered when determining admission to the major.

## Course Materials {.unnumbered}

Do not sell or distribute questions or answers to any assignment, quiz, or exam,
or other course materials given out on Canvas.
The lecture notes on this site are open,
under the license on the [home page](../index.qmd).
